title: Range Sum Query - Mutable
statement:
Design a class `NumArray` that keeps an integer array and serves two kinds of requests, arriving in any order:

- `NumArray(nums)` stores the starting array `nums`.
- `update(index, val)` overwrites the element at position `index` with `val`.
- `sumRange(left, right)` returns the total of the elements at positions `left` through `right`, counting both ends (`left <= right`), using the array as it stands after all earlier updates.
constraints: At most 3 * 10^4 calls in total are made to update and sumRange
notes:
## Intuition

Keeping the plain array makes `update` instant but forces `sumRange` to add up to n values; keeping prefix sums flips that cost onto `update`. A segment tree balances the two. Each internal node stores the sum of a block of the array, the blocks halve at every level, and any range is covered by O(log n) whole blocks. Changing one element only touches the blocks that contain it: one per level.

## Approach

1. Store the tree in an array `tree` of length `2n`. The leaves `tree[n..2n-1]` hold `nums`; node `node` has children `2 * node` and `2 * node + 1`.
2. Fill the internal nodes from `n - 1` down to `1`, each as the sum of its two children.
3. `update`: write `val` into leaf `index + n`, then walk to the root (`node / 2`) recomputing each parent.
4. `sumRange`: use a half-open window `[low, high)` over the leaves. While it is not empty: if `low` is odd (a right child), add `tree[low]` alone and step past it; if `high` is odd, the last node inside, `high - 1`, is a left child, so step back onto it and add it alone. Then halve both to move up one level.

## Example 1, step by step

With `nums = [1, 3, 5]`, `n = 3` and the leaves are `tree[3..5] = 1, 3, 5`. Then `tree[2] = 3 + 5 = 8` and `tree[1] = 8 + 1 = 9`. `sumRange(0, 2)` starts with `low = 3, high = 6`: `low` is odd, so `sum = 1` and `low = 4`; going up gives `low = 2, high = 3`; `high` is odd, so it becomes 2 and `sum = 1 + 8 = 9`. `update(1, 2)` sets `tree[4] = 2`, then `tree[2] = 7` and `tree[1] = 8`. The second `sumRange(0, 2)` adds `tree[3] = 1` and `tree[2] = 7`, returning `8`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) to build; O(log n) per `update` and `sumRange`, since each climbs one level per step.
- Space: O(n) for `tree`.

## Pitfalls

- `right` is inclusive, so the window's end is `right + n + 1`.
- In `sumRange`, decrement `high` before reading `tree[high]`; `high` itself is outside the window.
- `update` must replace the leaf, not add `val` to it: `val` is the new value, not a change.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums`; leaves start at `tree[n]` |
| `tree` | segment tree; `tree[node]` is the sum of its two children |
| `node` | current tree position while building or updating |
| `low`, `high` | half-open window `[low, high)` of nodes still to cover |
| `sum` | total of the blocks already added |

narration.3: Remember how many elements there are; the leaves start at position n.
narration.4: Allocate 2n slots: n leaves plus n - 1 internal nodes (slot 0 is unused).
narration.5: Copy every element of nums into its leaf.
narration.8: Build parents from the bottom up so both children are ready first.
narration.9: A parent's value is the sum of its two children.
narration.14: Find the leaf that holds position index.
narration.15: Overwrite that leaf with the new value.
narration.16: Climb until the root has been fixed.
narration.18: ...and recompute it from its two children.
narration.23: The window starts at the leaf for left...
narration.24: ...and ends just after the leaf for right, so it is half-open.
narration.26: Keep going while some part of the range is still uncovered.
narration.27: low is odd, so it is a right child whose parent would reach before the range.
narration.28: Add this block on its own...
narration.31: high is odd, so the last node inside the window is a left child whose parent would reach past the range.
narration.35: Move the left edge up one level.
narration.36: Move the right edge up one level.
narration.38: Every block in the range has been added.
